podcast.title: Attempt to Regain Group Name and Death
podcast.body: Catherine Anderson (Jean Caffin) was actively pursuing a lawsuit under the Truth in Music Act to regain ownership of The Marvelettes' name, which Motown had sold off, when she died of a stroke in 2011. This legal action highlighted the struggle of original members to control their legacy. "Jean Caffin were in the process of suing to regain the name under the Truth in Music Act, when she died of a stroke in 2011."

podcast.title: Exclusion from Motown Anniversaries
podcast.body: Despite her contributions, Catherine Anderson was not invited to any of Motown's major anniversary celebrations, a consistent oversight for the original members of the label's first number one group. "None of the members of the first group to hit number one on the label were invited to be part of any of them."

podcast.title: Group Role and Financial Management
podcast.body: Within The Marvelettes, Catherine Anderson served as the group's spokesperson for interviews and was responsible for managing their money, indicating a practical and articulate role within the ensemble. "Catherine was a spokesperson in interviews, and looked after the group's money"

podcast.title: Refusal for Album Cover Appearance
podcast.body: When Motown sought to feature her on the cover photograph for Wonder Young's 1970 solo album "The Return of The Marvelettes," Catherine Anderson refused. She stated that if she wasn't considered good enough to sing on the record, she wouldn't appear on its cover. "She told her label that if she wasn't good enough to sing on the record, she wasn't good enough to appear on the cover either, and so the cover, like the record, only featured Wanda of the original Marvillette."
